content: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for the development of several cancers, including breast, colon, and gynecologic carcinomas1,2. Recent evidence has shown that obesity not only contributes to carcinogenesis but also affects the prognosis of patients with various types of cancer. For instance, obesity has been associated with poorer outcomes in breast3,4 and colon cancers5,6. In contrast, some studies have reported a paradoxical survival advantage in obese patients with gastric7 or renal8 cancers.
